rationale: The open gap on the configuration-recovery question asks whether a recovered stale configuration can change a decision that is observable outside the node. A local construction run of the new three-node harness showed exactly that, so this batch registers the fixed experiment that measures it: after A restarts with RestoreCommittedLogs on it tracks the snapshot's three-voter configuration, wins an election with only the removed server reachable, and commits an entry that the committed two-voter configuration never got.

scope.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C on one another's transports. A snapshots while {A,B,C} is committed; the leader then removes C, which commits against {A,B}, and commits three more entries. A is shut down and restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over the same stores, while B is disconnected from A and C. The harness reports A's tracked configuration, whether A wins the election, and for a command applied after that: the client result, A's commit and applied index, whether A's FSM applied the payload, and whether the entry is present in A's, B's and C's logs.
assumptions: The removed server C keeps running and keeps answering AppendEntries, which is what a removal without shutting the process down leaves in place; the harness does not simulate C being killed.

A's snapshot is taken through the normal snapshot goroutine while the committed configuration is still {A,B,C}, so its configuration index is the bootstrap entry's index and its configuration contains C.
B is partitioned before A is restarted, so the committed configuration's only other voter cannot contribute an acknowledgement.
The nodes are in-memory transports and stores in one process; leadership, terms and quorum arithmetic are the real code paths.
excluded: No process-level restart, no production log store, and no attempt to complete the downstream loss of the entry; the predicate stops at the commitment rule.
No case in which the restarted node is the only stale voter or in which the stale configuration excludes a voter rather than including a removed one.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values: NewInmemTransport with a random address each, inmemConfig with LocalID = 'server-' + address and RestoreCommittedLogs true for every node, plus NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore per node. All transports are connected pairwise; BootstrapCluster is called on each node with the same three-voter configuration; NewRaft is called for each with a fresh MockFSM. The harness then waits for a real leader, applies one command through it, and takes a user snapshot on A through A.raft.Snapshot() while {A,B,C} is committed. It calls RemoveServer(C) on the leader and waits for that future, then applies three more commands, and records A's staged commit index, last index and the newest configuration entry in A's log. A is shut down and B is disconnected from A's transport and C's transport; a new transport bound to A's old address is created and connected to C only. NewRaft is called again on A's stores with RestoreCommittedLogs true and a fresh MockFSM. The harness reads A's tracked configurations through r.configurationsCh, waits up to five seconds for A to lead, and if it does, applies the payload 'stale-quorum-entry' with a two second timeout, then samples A's log entry term, the same index in B's and C's logs, A's commit and applied indexes, and A's FSM log contents.
experiment.responsibility: raft's leader is responsible for committing an entry only when a majority of the configuration it is bound to has stored it, and raft's startup recovery is responsible for binding the leader to the configuration the committed log establishes rather than to an older one.

comparisons.description: Where the restart that tracks the snapshot's older three-voter configuration became leader while its log's committed configuration has two voters, committing an entry that its FSM applied and the client accepted while the committed configuration's other voter lacks it is a violation; such a witness shows the commit was decided by the removed server. Where A did not lead, the antecedent is false and nothing is claimed.
